description: Verify that a D2 button toggles the D13 LED (off after reset, toggles on each press, debounced to exactly one toggle per bouncy press, reacts quickly) and that each toggle is reported as ON/OFF over Serial1 at 9600 baud.

steps.requirement: The LED is off right after reset, with the button not pressed.
The LED turns on quickly after the first button press.
After the first press turns the LED on, the board prints ON on its own line on Serial1 at 9600 baud.
After the first press the LED stays steadily on (it toggled exactly once).
After the second press turns the LED off, the board prints OFF on its own line on Serial1.
The second press toggles the LED back off.
A single bouncy press toggles the LED exactly once, no matter how many bounce edges occur.

not_graded.requirement: Implement debouncing in software, without blocking delay() calls.
not_graded.reason: Whether the implementation uses delay() or is purely software-timed is a code-structure detail that cannot be determined from electrical signals alone.
Code comments are a style requirement not observable through any electrical measurement.

assumptions: The handout gives no numeric limit for 'quick' LED reaction, so we require the LED to change within 50 ms of the button's falling edge.
The handout gives no bounce profile, so we simulate a bouncy press with 5 edges at 2 ms (2000 us) intervals, typical of mechanical switch bounce, ending at the pressed (low) level.
The debounce-check window of 300 ms is sized to cover the bounce duration plus any reasonable software debounce delay and the LED's reaction, while still only accepting exactly one toggle.
uart framing_errors is expected to be exactly 0 on each serial check, confirming the student used the specified 9600 baud rate.

Each toggle is verified by letting the button rest in the new pressed/released state after the stimulus, then sampling LED steadiness (edge_count 0) and final level, rather than catching the exact transition, to avoid stacking a conflicting concurrent measurement on the same pin as the edge_delay/uart checks.
